newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dollar surge sends German shares to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Dollar surge sends German shares to new highs.

text.p: German shares surged to fresh record highs as bourse trade opened on Wednesday and dealers said new orders were streaming into the market following the dollar's surge against the mark.

The blue-chip DAX index, building on gains from IBIS electronic trading following Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to Congress on Tuesday, was up 61.34 points or more than two percent at 3,038.05 points.
The surge came after the dollar rose above 1.63 marks and after a strong performance by Japanese stocks and Wall Street.
Virtually all German blue chips were higher as dealers said not all investors had adapted their portfolios yet to a brighter earnings outlook, especially for German exporters.
"It's hard to predict the dynamics of this market just now," said one dealer, who said he saw the DAX hitting 3,070 points in the short term.

The gains had started after Greenspan's testimony calmed fears about a risk of an imminent rate hike. Markets read his comments to mean that while the U.S. central bank did see some signs of inflation, it was unlikely to take immediate action.

Bank stocks remained ahead, with Dresdner Bank up 1.45 marks at 54.65 marks after a newspaper report that it was seeking to buy a U.K. fund management unit. Recent favourite Deutsche Bank AG rose another 3.15 marks to 83.65.
Industrial group Daimler-Benz AG, one of the DAX's most dollar sensitive shares, was up 2.90 marks at 115.50.
Some moves were sparked by the bourse's announcement of a reshuffle of its MDAX mid-cap index.

Automobile firm Kiekert AG was the biggest gainer in percentage terms, rising eight percent to 60.50 marks while speciality chemicals frim Ruetgerswerke was the biggest loser, with a drop of nearly six percent to 227 marks.
Kiekert, along with dialysis group Fresenius Medical Care, insurer Hannover Re and preference shares of financial group MLP are to join the MDAX from March 24.
To make way for them, Ruetgerswerke, windows manufacturer Weru AG, utility VEW AG and footwear retailer Salamander will leave the 70-share index.
Generally, inclusion in an index boosts a stock because the move promises greater liquidity while removal from an index tends to weigh on the share price.
